# Why you cannot connect to a remote computer, and how to fix it

Written for: Support staff and IT administrators diagnosing a remote session that will not establish at all.

Written by the 247connect Marketing Team · Last reviewed 27 August 2026

In short

A failed remote connection is almost always one of four things: the device is off or asleep, the agent is not running, something on the network is blocking the outbound connection, or your credentials are being rejected. Work through them in that order. Each check rules out a whole class of cause, so you narrow the problem in four steps instead of guessing at settings.

## Key takeaways

  * Diagnose in layers: power, agent, network, credentials. Guessing at settings wastes the most time.
  * A device showing offline in the console has not necessarily failed — it may be asleep, on a different network, or waiting on a captive portal.
  * Modern remote support tools connect outbound over 443, so an inbound firewall rule is rarely the cause; an outbound proxy or TLS inspection often is.
  * An error that mentions credentials, permission or authorisation is a different problem from one that times out. Do not treat them the same.
  * Record what fixed it. The same device usually fails the same way twice.

## Step one: prove the device is actually on

It sounds trivial, and it is the single most common answer. A desktop that has gone into sleep or hibernation, a laptop closed on a desk, a machine someone switched off at the wall over the weekend — none of these are reachable, and no amount of configuration will change that.

Check the last-seen timestamp in your console before anything else. A device that was online an hour ago and is now unreachable tells a very different story from one that has not checked in for three weeks.

  * Last-seen time in the management console
  * Whether the machine is on a power plan that sleeps the network adapter
  * Whether wake-on-LAN is configured and the machine is on a wired connection
  * Whether anyone on site can confirm the power light

# Remote Is Not Telework: What 93,496 Federal Announcements Show

Only 142 of 93,496 analyzed 2026 announcements were confirmed remote. Another 12,860 were telework eligible but not remote.

By Nadia Belamin

Published August 17, 2026 Last edited August 20, 2026

## Quick Read

About a 30-second read

Only 142 of 93,496 analyzed 2026 federal announcements were confirmed remote. Another 12,860 were telework eligible but still tied to an official duty station.

Remote and telework are not synonyms. Remote positions generally establish a worksite away from the agency office, while telework requires reporting to the named duty station under the agency's arrangement; unknown or ambiguous records remain separate.

Applicants should verify the location field and announcement language before assuming work can be performed from anywhere. A telework signal may offer flexibility, but it does not erase commuting, locality-pay or reporting requirements.

## Full Analysis

Share this article

Use the canonical article URL for social posts, email, or citations.

[Button: Copy link]LinkedInRedditEmailXBluesky

A federal job that permits telework is not automatically a remote job. In 93,496 2026 announcements with current-source remote fields, FederalHiringData found 142 confirmed remote announcements and 12,860 telework-eligible announcements that were not marked remote.

Confirmed remote represented 0.2% of this cohort. Telework-eligible but not remote represented 13.8%. The remaining 80,494 were on-site or did not carry a positive remote/telework signal.

Image: Bar chart comparing confirmed remote, telework eligible and on-site or unspecified announcements

## OPM's definitions explain the difference

OPM defines telework as an arrangement in which an employee works from an approved alternative site on scheduled days and also regularly works at an agency site. Remote work is different: the employee is not expected to report to an agency worksite on a regular and recurring basis under the remote-work agreement.

That is why FederalHiringData keeps separate filters. Combining both categories and labeling the result "remote jobs" would inflate the number of positions that are actually advertised as fully remote.

## The current snapshot is just as lopsided

Among 11,983 records in the warehouse that were still open on Aug. 17, only 29 were confirmed remote. 3,280 were telework eligible but not remote.

Those counts are a dated snapshot, not a promise that the same jobs remain open now. Readers should use the live remote and telework filters and check the announcement's location and telework sections before applying.

## The agency pattern shows why one label can mislead

Veterans Health Administration accounted for 76 confirmed remote and 2,501 telework-eligible, non-remote announcements in the 2026 cohort. Veterans Benefits Administration followed with 23 remote and 291 telework-eligible announcements. Small counts can move sharply when only a few announcements are added or closed.

The occupation mix also demonstrates why "remote federal work" is not synonymous with federal IT. Only one 2210 announcement in this 2026 cohort was confirmed remote, even though 840 were telework eligible. Clinical records, medical and trainee series supplied more of the confirmed-remote count. A keyword-only search for technology roles would miss that structure.

## Why this is not a disappearance trend

FederalHiringData cannot honestly use the full 2017-2026 archive to chart remote-work disappearance. The complete historical archive preserves dates, titles, grades, pay and occupations, but its older source does not carry a consistently comparable remote indicator. Current-source remote fields are complete for 2026 and sparse before 2025.

The defensible result is a cross-section: remote was rare in the 2026 records with reliable status fields, and telework was much more common. A causal or long-run trend claim would require a consistently populated field across years.

## How applicants should read an announcement

Check the overview's location, remote and telework fields together. Then read any agency-specific conditions. A telework-eligible label may still involve several days per pay period at a duty station. A remote label can still restrict the employee's approved worksite or geographic area. Neither arrangement is an entitlement, and the announcement remains the controlling source.

## Methodology and limitations

FederalHiringData analyzed active and historical `Job` source records opened in 2026 through Aug. 14. Confirmed remote requires the normalized remote indicator to be true. Telework eligible excludes records already counted as remote. The active snapshot required a close date on or after Aug. 17. Counts are announcements, not hires or positions.

## How the live record check works

The live record check re-derives content digests, Merkle inclusion and signatures against pinned public keys. The checks run server-side on read-only evidence copies fetched at pinned object generations. The check never writes, never signs, and never lists storage.

Reading the result

## Four states, kept distinct

A record check is read one dimension at a time. UNKNOWN is not VERIFIED. FAILED is not a warning. NOT CHECKED is not FAILED.

  * VERIFIED

The dimension was checked and the check passed. Verification is reported per dimension; dimensions are never reduced to a single overall result.

  * FAILED

The dimension was checked and did not pass. Failure codes are reported verbatim, never softened into a warning.

  * UNKNOWN

The dimension could not be determined. An unknown is reported as unknown — it is never presented as verified.

  * NOT CHECKED

The dimension was not run. An absent check is stated as absent, never counted as a pass.

## Limitations

This page publishes one recorded decision only. Population completeness is not proven. Governance completeness is not proven. Organizational independence is not claimed. SOFTWARE KMS protection is not HSM protection.

A content digest by itself is a checksum, not a signature. Where this page names a signature class, an authoritative signature over the stated digest exists in the published record facts; nothing here treats a bare checksum as one.

## Issue Details

I am trying to check remote system status from TestStand using the Check Remote System Status step and I am getting the following error. How should I resolve it?
LabVIEW: The network connection was closed by the peer. If you are using the Open VI Reference function on a remote VI Server connection, verify that the machine is allowed access by selecting Tools>>Options>>VI Server on the server side.
Image: image.png

## Solution

Performing the following steps in the remote system should solve this issue.

  1. In LabVIEW of the remote system, click Tools >> Options >> VI Server.
  2. Click Add under Machine Access and insert * as the value of the Machine name/address.
  3.   4. Click OK to close the Options dialogue boxImage: image.png

## Additional Information

This error happens because the local system is not able to access the remote system.

It could also be related to connection instability. Please ping your target and make sure it responds correctly.

If Chrome Remote Desktop shows your computer as offline and gives the “failed to start” error, it usually means the host service isn’t running properly on the remote device.

A few quick things to try:

  * Restart the remote computer (this often fixes the host service)
  * Turn Remote Access OFF and set it up again from remotedesktop.google.com
  * Make sure Google Chrome is up to date on both devices
  * Check firewall/antivirus isn’t blocking the service
  * Confirm you’re signed into the same Google account

If it still shows offline after this, removing the device and re-adding it usually resolves the issue.

# General

## Questions and answers

### 

Is there a difference between remote work and telework?

Yes. For purposes of OPM’s guidance, telework refers to arrangements where the employee is expected to report to work both at an agency worksite and alternative worksite on a regular and recurring basis each pay period. Remote work does not involve an expectation that the employee regularly reports to the agency worksite each pay period. Remote work is an arrangement that an agency, in its discretion, may choose to undertake, if the arrangement is consistent with the agency’s needs and the duties of the given position. A remote work arrangement may be initiated by the agency posting the position as one that will be performed remotely or by an employee requesting the privilege of working remotely. Agencies may determine whether to grant such requests on a case-by-case basis. The remote work agreement must accurately document the employee’s worksite to enable accurate determination of locality pay. Given budget implications, equity considerations, and other factors, agency remote work policies should clearly outline the level of approval required to institute or execute a remote work agreement or position.

OPM will be publishing a Remote Work Guide to further explain the implications, considerations, and strategies for the appropriate use of remote work.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Introduction

When something's wrong with a Level agent — a device showing offline, remote connections not working, or an automation failing — the diagnostic command and the automation step output are the two places to start. Level's watchdog handles keeping the service running automatically, so in most cases you're looking for a connectivity or configuration issue, not a service problem.


# Running the Diagnostic Command

If a device is showing offline in Level but is actually powered on and connected, run `--check` on the affected device. It outputs a structured report covering the agent, system info, Level service state, connection checks, sleep settings, and active operations.

Windows  | `& 'C:\Program Files\Level\level.exe' --check`
macOS  | `sudo /usr/local/bin/level --check`
Linux  | `sudo /usr/local/bin/level --check`
